title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: usage reports for Copilot Search, connectors and agents in US Government clouds
summary: The briefing passes: its government-cloud scope and target match the roadmap, and the reporting paths and Graph operations are documented. Minor corrections should complete the reporting route, remove request bodies from the displayed calls, and replace the unnecessary caveat about role assignments.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans new Copilot Search usage reports for US Government customers.
claims.quote: We are introducing new Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports for Copilot Search, Copilot Connectors, and Copilot Agents for US Government customers

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Usage report access depends on the administrator's reporting role.
claims.quote: To view usage reports, you must have one of the following permissions: ... Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details). ... Reports Reader ... AI Administrator

claims.claim: The reporting options page lists AI Administrator as a role that accesses Copilot reports.
claims.quote: AI Administrator: Accesses the Copilot reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; controls[1].note
claims.claim: The organisation's report privacy setting governs whether user, group and site names are concealed.
claims.quote: By default, all reports hide user information such as usernames, display names, groups, and sites to help companies support local privacy laws.

claims.claim: Copilot reports are reached at Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: To view reports, go to Reports > Usage. ... Select Microsoft Copilot > Readiness or Usage
claims.fix: The path stops at the report family. Replace it with 'Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Usage' for the usage report documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/copilot-admin-reports.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments assigns a directory role using principalId, roleDefinitionId and directoryScopeId.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments ... "roleDefinitionId": "c2cf284d-6c41-4e6b-afac-4b80928c9034", "principalId": "f8ca5a85-489a-49a0-b555-0a6d81e56f0d", "directoryScopeId": "/"
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call to 'POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments', and name principalId, roleDefinitionId and directoryScopeId in the note instead of printing the request body.

claims.claim: The directory role-assignment API assigns a role rather than opening a report.
claims.quote: Create a new unifiedRoleAssignment object. ... Create a role assignment for the directory provider

claims.claim: The documented general role-assignment operation is presented with a caveat that Microsoft has not confirmed it as a control specific to these reports.
claims.quote: To use the reporting features described in this article, you need to sign into different portals with the appropriate permissions. ... AI Administrator: Accesses the Copilot reports.
claims.fix: Replace the unconfirmed-applicability sentence with 'Assigning a reporting role controls access; the reporting options page lists AI Administrator as able to access Copilot reports.' Keep the distinction that the API assigns the role rather than opening the report.

claims.claim: Name concealment is configured at Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings updates report name concealment using displayConcealedNames.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings ... { "displayConcealedNames": true }
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call to 'PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings'. Add 'The request body sets displayConcealedNames.' to its note and retain the explanation of true and false.

claims.claim: displayConcealedNames true conceals names and false shows identifiable information.
claims.quote: If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: Beta Graph APIs are subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.
